blocks.text: The two-branch binding study launched at 13:04 UTC on 26 October 2026 after data checks and limited-run preparation. This post records launch, not the separate finished results.

The idea was that more varied taught values might help choose the requested object and date. Both branches kept 3,000 standard conversations and restarted from the same self-trained 100-million-token base with fresh optimizers. Each added 500 task-repair rows.

The control repeated 100 base cases five times. The varied branch used a control plus changed requested year, changed title, renamed target, and reordered returned items for each. Half changed only the deadline; half explicitly renamed and updated the task. Stored dates did not change in year variants. Old and new titles were sampled independently to avoid an easy fixed-prefix clue.

Both branches had 3,500 rows, but repetition had 3,100 distinct histories and varied values 3,500. One row pass had 524,402 versus 524,382 assistant targets. Planned complete-conversation totals were 1,999,908 versus 1,999,822, both in 13,338 steps. Equal rows did not give identical exposure.

Added rows supplied about 15.23% of targets in each branch. Equal row counts did not mean equal distinct histories or target counts. This tests a stated package of value changes, not a new loss rule or pairing alone.

The first production build stopped because a test title already appeared in retained training. No final input record was committed and training had not started. The fix changed test-title number sampling, not training, while keeping exact title and history exclusions. It happened before model results existed.

The successful build passed 44 focused CPU tests and replayed saved old and new conversations. It found no exact test-title or complete-history matches with training. The longest full training conversation was 995 tokens, below context 1,536. Cutting examples short was not allowed.
All added text was recorded as original CC0 material. No outside teacher, general-text collection, or third-party model weights were added.

The model still had 97,536,768 values, using BF16 projection calculations and FP32 stored weights and Adam state. Each branch had a 3,600-second trainer limit and 3,780-second outer guard. Saves were scheduled every 100,000 targets or 300 seconds. The absolute cutoff stayed 31 October 2026 at 04:12 UTC.

Eighteen limited evaluation jobs were planned: the new 64 cases, branch-specific fit, original calibration, known development sets, and paired checks. Raw/guarded views and related base cases were explicitly treated as correlated. The control's 50-row added-training sample contained only ten distinct repeated histories; the varied sample had 50 distinct histories.

Resource observation had failed and partial attempts, leaving early and middle training gaps. This launch record cannot establish full-run peak memory. Launch success gives no quality result or reason to promote a model.
This AI-assisted summary was checked against the fixed production inputs, preflight reviews, budgets, and launch records. Private runtime identities and raw logs stay out of the journal.
